summary: W. G. Emrich, Director of the Office of Environment and Design at FHWA, submitted a memorandum dated September 24, 1976 forwarding the final negative declaration/Section 4(f) statement to Washington and explicitly recommending approval of the Section 4(f) statement for the temporary use of minor amounts of Section 4(f) lands. His office supported the project's finding that there are no feasible and prudent alternatives to the temporary use of Woodrow Wilson Woods land and that all possible planning to minimize harm had been included.
complaint_summary: Emrich forwards the final negative declaration/Section 4(f) statement and recommends approval of the temporary use of Section 4(f) lands from Woodrow Wilson Woods for the US-30 reconstruction project.

statement.text:
Attached are four (4) copies of the final negative declaration/Section 4(f) statement for the proposed subject highway improvement. The statement is being forwarded to your office for approval of the temporary use of minor amounts of Section 4(f) lands.
A draft EIS was circulated for the proposed action (FHWA-ILL-EIS-72-16-D) and subsequently changed to a negative declaration on December 30, 1975 in accordance with paragraph 13p of FHPM 7-7-2.
The proposed use of Section 4(f) lands involves only a temporary easement to reconstruct a headwall for a culvert that carries Thorn Creek under US-30, and a temporary easement to reconstruct the entrance to a parking area for the Section 4(f) lands. The areas within the easements, except for the paved entrance to the parking area, will be reshaped, topsoiled and sodded to restore the lands to their original state.
The statement has been reviewed by Regional Counsel and their review has been forwarded to FHWA Chief Counsel.
We have reviewed the statement and recommend your approval of the Section 4(f) statement.
Attachment
W. G. EMRICH, DIRECTOR
OFFICE OF ENVIRONMENT AND DESIGN
